newsitem.title: USA: Audit finds Mass. lottery officials partied hearty.
newsitem.headline: Audit finds Mass. lottery officials partied hearty.

text.p: Massachusetts Treasurer and Republican gubernatorial contender Joe Malone spent $145,000 from the state's lottery on symphony tickets, golf outings and parties, a state audit has found, according to reports.

The Boston Herald and the Boston Globe say the explosive report, to be released this week by Massachusetts Auditory Joseph DeNucci, claims the Lottery was billed for $145,000 in 1995 alone for the various functions.
The expenses were concealed in an account code-named the "doughnut fund" by Lottery officials, according to the newspapers.
Malone, who is preparing a bid for the 1998 gubernatorial race, was not immediately available for comment Tuesday, but both papers reported he declined to discuss the audit's finding with them.
The audit reportedly also found Scientific Games Inc, which has a $48 million contract for instant game tickets, overcharged the Lottery by $700,000.
